questions.title: jQuery selectors
questions.prompt:
jQuery is loaded. Using jQuery selectors and the `text()` method:

1. Set the text of the element with id `title` to `Selected!`.
2. Add the class `highlight` to every element with class `tip` **inside** `#tips`.
3. Store the number of `<li>` elements on the page in `itemCount`.

setup.html:
Title

  • Use ids for single elements
  • Plain item
  • Use classes for groups

Outside tip
setup.css:
body { font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; padding: 1em; }
.highlight { background: #fff3a0; }

hints: A jQuery object has a length property.

tests.name: Only the 2 tips in #tips are highlighted

questions.title: Stripe a table with :even
questions.prompt: Using jQuery's filter selectors, add the class `stripe` to the **even-numbered** rows (0, 2, 4…) of the table **body**, and add the class `first` to the **first** cell of every row in the body.
hints: $("tbody td:first-child") selects the first cell of each row (td:first would select only one cell).

tests.name: Rows 0 and 2 of the body are striped
tests.code:
const rows = $("#scores tbody tr");
return rows.eq(0).hasClass("stripe") && rows.eq(2).hasClass("stripe") && !rows.eq(1).hasClass("stripe") && !rows.eq(3).hasClass("stripe");

tests.name: The header row is not striped
Each body row's first cell has class "first"

questions.title: Chain jQuery methods
questions.prompt: In **one statement** that **chains** three methods on `$("#notice")`: set its text to `Sale today!`, add the class `alert`, and set its CSS `font-size` to `24px`.

setup.css:
body { font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; padding: 1em; }
.alert { color: #c0392b; }

hints: Most jQuery methods return the jQuery object, so you can call another method right after: $(...).a().b().c();

tests.name: Text, class and font-size are set
tests.code:
const n = $("#notice");
return n.text() === "Sale today!" && n.hasClass("alert") && n.css("font-size") === "24px";

questions.title: The ready event and $(this)
questions.prompt: Inside a **ready** event handler, attach a `click` handler to every `<li>` in `#menu`. When an item is clicked, give **it** the class `selected` and remove that class from all the other items. Use `$(this)`.
hints: Inside a regular function handler, this is the clicked element. $(this).siblings() gets the others.

questions.title: each() to build a list
questions.prompt: Use `$.each()` (or `.each()`) to go through the `books` array and **append** an `<li>` to `#books` for each, with text like `Dune (1965)`. Then use `.each()` on the new items to add the class `old` to books from before 1970.

setup.css:
body { font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; padding: 1em; }
.old { font-style: italic; }

tests.name: Books before 1970 have class "old"
tests.code:
const li = $("#books li");
return li.eq(0).hasClass("old") && !li.eq(1).hasClass("old") && li.eq(2).hasClass("old");

questions.title: Email List with jQuery
questions.prompt:
Like the chapter's Email List application, written with jQuery: on the form's `submit` event, show errors in the `<span>` after each field and cancel the submit if any:

- `#email` empty → `This field is required.`
- `#email2` not equal to `#email` → `Emails must match.`
- `#first` empty → `This field is required.`

Fields are trimmed, and a field with no error has an empty span.
hints: $("#email").next() is the span after the field.

tests.name: Empty form shows required messages and cancels
tests.code:
const ok = document.getElementById("email_form").dispatchEvent(new Event("submit", { cancelable: true }));
return ok === false && $("#email").next().text() === "This field is required." && $("#first").next().text() === "This field is required.";

tests.name: Mismatched emails are reported
A valid form submits with no messages
